answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may submit jobs or vote, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Creating a thousand sybils no longer means merely generating usernames: the attacker must fund a thousand locks and risks losing them for each detected lie. Audits must sample work across identities, since one stake cannot prove a person is unique; onyx, gale, and opal can each name a registered agent, but none gets a free vote. This raises the attack’s capital cost without claiming to eliminate sybils.
